route.title: Descending board potential and prime-valuation gcd invariance
route.mathematicalIdea: Use the complete proof.md. A move weakly decreases both the board product and the number of entries greater than one; it strictly decreases the product when the chosen gcd exceeds one, and strictly decreases the count when the gcd is one. Their sum is a well-founded potential. Every reachable board remains positive with product greater than one. For each prime, a move replaces valuations r,s by min(r,s), |r-s| and therefore preserves their gcd; it also preserves the prime support of the board product. Thus Mval is invariant. On a terminal board, all entries except its unique M>1 are one, so prime factorization identifies Mval with M. Assemble all five published claims without treating any as an assumption.
orderedMilestones: Prove preservation of positive entries, board cardinality, and product greater than one under Move; establish strict descent of product plus large-entry count.
Use well-founded induction for finite terminal reachability and prove a reachable terminal board has exactly one entry greater than one.
Prove prime-support preservation and the per-prime valuation-gcd identity for a single Move, then lift Mval invariance through Reachable.
Evaluate Mval on a terminal board using unique prime factorization, derive choice independence and Mval_gt_one, and close the five-way conjunction.
assumptionsUsed: Only IsInitial for the starting board, Reachable and IsTerminal where those are binders of the published claims, and the stated definitions of Board, Move, gExp, and Mval.
mathematicalRisks: The product alone does not strictly decrease for coprime m,n; the large-entry count supplies the missing descent.
Equal selected values still represent two distinct positions in the multiset decomposition.
Zero valuations from entries equal to one must not be confused with a zero gcd of positive valuations.
Terminal evaluation requires the reachable-board positivity invariant; it cannot assume all nonlarge entries are one without ruling out zero.
No published solution.lean or unproved conjunct may be imported as a certificate.
